subject: Alleged inference degradation — final update and closure
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@pineboxretail.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent slow responses and truncated outputs during peak traffic

Hi Redwood support,

We saw a spike in latency around 15:30 PST today where several inference calls to model 'redwood-13b-v2' returned in ~6s instead of the usual ~350ms, and a handful of responses appeared truncated (cut off mid-sentence). This impacted checkout recommendations on our site for ~12 minutes.

Attached is a representative request payload and a snippet from our frontend logs. Can you confirm whether there was any degradation on your side? This is on our production workspace (pinebox-prod).

Thanks,
Emma Li
Senior Platform Engineer
PineBox Retail

Attachments: pinebox-sample-payload.json, request-snippet-20270508.txt
From: support@redwood.com
To: Emma Li <emma.li@pineboxretail.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent slow responses and truncated outputs during peak traffic

Hi Emma — thanks for the report and the samples. We opened SUP-9821 to track this. Quick updates from initial triage:

- We correlated your request IDs with our ingress logs and saw no cluster-wide queueing or OOM events at 15:30 PST.
- A small number of requests from your workspace experienced higher token generation time; the majority were within expected latency distributions.
- The attached server trace shows two requests that had repeated client reconnects and 3xx retries prior to final completion. Those reconnects can make the end-to-end time look higher even when our runtime processed tokens at normal speed.

Next steps: Monica (platform operations) will run a deeper KV-cache/worker-affinity trace and we will also ask for a full client-side HAR for the period if possible. Could you confirm whether you have any edge proxies or retries configured for the /v1/streams endpoint?

We’ll follow up with concrete evidence or a closure note by Monday.

— Redwood Support
Support Engineer: Monica Patel
redwood.com/support

Attachments: redwood-trace-20270508.log
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SUP-9821 — summary of reproduction attempts / no systemic issue found

Quick internal summary for the sales/escalation thread:

- Reproductions: Ran a 30-minute replay of PineBox sample traffic against the regional fleet that handled their requests. We drove burst profiles matching their request timestamps.
- Observations: Token-level generation time distribution stayed within normal percentiles (p50~120ms/p95~480ms for this model under that load tier). We saw two sessions where the client performed early connection resets and retried the same request with backoff. Those sequences explain the large apparent end-to-end durations in the customer's logs.
- Truncation: The responses flagged as truncated match the pattern of client-side stream cancellation (frontend closed socket after perceived delay) — the full output exists in our final event for those requests.
- Platform health: No worker crashes, memory pressure, or autoscaler anomalies in the customer's region during the window.

Recommendation: Close as 'no confirmed platform degradation' and offer a joint debugging call to walk PineBox through client-side retry behavior and to collect HARs. Offer a short-term monitoring check and provide a test key to run controlled traces.

I can draft the closure email to the customer and include the evidence snippets.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Platform Operations Engineer
redwood.com
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Emma Li <emma.li@pineboxretail.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final update on the reported slow responses / truncated outputs (SUP-9821)

Hi Emma — following up with our final findings after a full triage. Thank you for the payload and snippets — they were helpful. Summary below and next steps: 

What we investigated
- We replayed your representative traffic against the exact fleet that served your workspace and traced the token generation and socket lifecycle for each request. We also checked autoscaler, worker telemetry, and error traces for the window you reported.

What we found
- No platform-level degradation detected. Worker and autoscaler metrics were within normal ranges and there were no OOMs or infra interruptions.
- Several of the slow responses in your frontend logs correspond to sequences where the client retried or re-opened the streaming connection before the initial stream finished. Those retries lead to longer observed end-to-end times even when our runtime processed tokens normally.
- The messages you flagged as truncated were completed on our side — their final, full output is present in the event logs. The truncation appears to be caused by early socket closure on the client.

What we recommend
- Schedule a 45-minute debug session where our ops engineer (Monica) will walk through the client-side traces (HARs) and your edge retries configuration.
- In the meantime, we can issue a short-lived debug API key scoped to your workspace so you can run controlled replay tests — let me know if you want this.

Attachments included: request-snippet-20270508.txt, redwood-trace-20270508.log

If you'd like us to keep the ticket open while you run additional tests, we can do that; otherwise we propose closing SUP-9821 as 'no confirmed platform degradation' and list the root cause as 'client-side retry/stream cancellation behavior'.

Thanks — and apologies for the disruption to checkout recommendations. We want to help prevent this moving forward.

Best,
Aditya Rao
